lede: Mountain Village takes up first reading of an ordinance that would pull Housing Authority fees out of municipal code and into an annually updated fee schedule — a structural shift in how affordable housing costs get set that's worth understanding before it moves further. Elsewhere, San Miguel County's Housing Code Update working group meets for its eighth session on Land Use Code changes aimed at clearing obstacles to workforce housing, the BOCC has a full plate including a view-plain MOU tied to a 1999 settlement, and HARC takes a look at a potential demolition and rebuild of its own meeting hall at Rebekah Hall.

notable.stake: Policy on subpar bedrooms in mitigation units could affect housing stock quality.
Prop 123-funded code changes could reshape how workforce housing gets built countywide.
Possible demolition of Town-owned Rebekah Hall — HARC's own meeting place — is under review.
MOU on 1999 view-plain settlement and Constitutional Amendment discussions before BOCC.
Two public hearings — a PUD and a parcel subdivision — open for public comment.
First reading: ordinance shifting MVHA fees out of municipal code changes how housing costs get set.
